evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted check (1104-1116) only requires positive and differing manager PIDs and nonempty/differing invocation IDs across the before/after snapshots; it never binds the two snapshots to the same boot. Both manager snapshots are the same snapshot shape used for reboot (the loop at 1143-1146 reads `.get("runs")` for manager and reboot snapshots alike, and reboot snapshots carry a top-level `boot_id`, see 1117-1124), so a boot ID is available in the manager pair. If the guest reboots after the restart command but before the second inspect, the new boot supplies a different manager PID and invocation ID, so manager_restarted passes even though the restart command was not what restarted the manager; the later planned-reboot checks (boot_id_changed and qemu_pid_unchanged) still pass, so the report yields a false positive. Adding a nonempty, equal boot_id requirement is a small routine correctness repair that keeps the existing PID and invocation-ID comparisons, not a disruptive behavior or architectural change.
